Bill number: HB1322
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1310
 By Johnson

 HOUSE BILL 1322

 By Lamberth

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 Chapter 13, relative to charter schools.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-104, is amended by deleting

subdivision (4) and substituting instead:

 (4) "Authorizer" means a local board of education, the Tennessee public charter

 school commission, or the achievement school district as defined in § 49-1-614, that

 makes decisions regarding approval, renewal, and revocation of a public charter school

 application or agreement;

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-104, is amended by adding

the following as a new subdivision:

 ( ) "Replication" means the creation of one (1) or more charter schools pursuant

 to the process authorized in § 49-13-137 that utilize the same academic focus of an

 existing charter school operated by a sponsor or governing body;

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-106(i), is amended by deleting

the subsection and substituting instead:

 (i) If a sponsor seeks to establish a new public charter school, including an

 opportunity charter school, then the sponsor must apply to the local board of education

 or to the commission, if direct application to the commission is authorized in this chapter.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-107(a), is amended by

deleting "department of education" and substituting instead "commission".

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-107(a), is amended by adding

the following language at the end of the subsection:

 The commission shall make letters of intent received by the commission available on its

 website no later than ten (10) days from the date on which the letter was received.

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-107(b), is amended by

deleting the language that precedes the colon ":" and substituting instead:

 On or before February 1 of the year preceding the year in which the proposed

 public charter school plans to begin operation, the sponsor seeking to establish a public

 charter school shall prepare and file with the authorizer an application using an

 application template developed by the state board of education in coordination with the

 commission. The authorizer shall report each application received by the authorizer to

 the commission no later than ten (10) days from the date on which the authorizer

 received the application. A completed application must provide the following information

 and documents

 SECTION 7. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108, is amended by deleting

subdivision (b)(4).

 SECTION 8. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108(b)(5), is amended by

deleting the language "Beginning immediately upon the repeal of subdivision (b)(4)" and

substituting instead the language "Beginning on January 1, 2021".

 SECTION 9. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108(b)(5)(D), is amended by

deleting the language "department of education's" and substituting instead "state board of

education's".

 SECTION 10. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108(g), is amended by

adding the language "and the commission" after "department of education".

 SECTION 11. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108(g), is amended by

adding the language "and the commission" after "provide the department".

 SECTION 12. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-108, is amended by deleting

the language "This section only applies to" in subdivision (b)(1) and substituting instead the

language "Subsections (b)-(d) only apply to" and by adding the following new subsections:

 (h)

 (1) Beginning on July 1, 2025, if the commission has overturned a local

 board of education's decision to deny a public charter school application on three

 (3) separate occasions within a three-consecutive-year period, then, for the five-

 consecutive-year period immediately following the date on which the commission

 overturned the board's third decision to deny a public charter school application

 within the last three (3) years, any sponsor that seeks to establish a new public

 charter school in that LEA may apply directly to the commission.

 (2) If a sponsor elects to apply directly to the commission pursuant to this

 subsection (h), then the application process must be conducted in accordance

 with § 49-13-107 and with the following:

 (A) The commission shall rule by resolution, at a regularly or

 specially called meeting, to approve or deny a public charter school

 application no later than ninety (90) days after the date on which the

 commission received the completed application. If the commission fails

 to approve or deny a public charter school application within ninety (90)

 days, then the public charter school application is deemed approved;

 (B) If the commission denies an application, then the grounds for

 denial must be stated in writing and must specify objective reasons for the

 denial. Upon receipt of the grounds for denial, the sponsor has thirty (30)

 days to submit an amended application to correct any deficiencies. Upon

 receipt of the amended application, the commission has sixty (60) days to

 deny or approve the amended application. If the commission fails to

 approve or deny the amended application within sixty (60) days, then the

 amended application is deemed approved;

 (C) If the commission approves an application, then the

 commission is the authorizer and LEA for that public charter school; and

 (D) The commission's decision is final and not subject to appeal.

 (3) After the five-consecutive-year period during which a sponsor may

apply directly to the commission for approval pursuant to this subsection (h), a

sponsor that seeks to establish a new public charter school must apply directly to

the local board of education unless the conditions in subdivision (h)(1) are met in

the future.

(i)

 (1) A public institution of higher education in this state that seeks to open

a public charter school may apply to the local board of education or directly to the

commission. If a public institution of higher education in this state elects to apply

directly to the commission for approval of its public charter school application,

then the application process must be conducted in accordance with § 49-13-107.

 (2) Notwithstanding § 49-13-113(d)(6), a public charter school sponsored

by a public institution of higher education in this state may give an enrollment

preference to children of the public institution of higher education's employees or

members of the institution's governing body, not to exceed twenty-five percent

(25%) of the public charter school's total enrollment.

 SECTION 13. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-110(d), is amended by

deleting the subsection and substituting instead:

 (d) The governing body of the public charter school may petition the authorizer

 to amend the charter agreement. The commission shall determine the timelines for

 approval and the appeal process. If the authorizer is the commission, then an appeal

 shall not be made of the commission's decision to deny a petition to amend the charter

 agreement. The governing body of a public charter school may petition the authorizer

 for voluntary termination of the charter agreement before the charter agreement expires.

 SECTION 14. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-111(a)(4), is amended by

deleting "Except as provided in § 49-13-142(d), receive" and substituting instead "Receive".

deleting "department" and substituting instead "state board".

deleting "department of education" and substituting instead "commission".

adding the following language at the end of the subsection:

 The commission shall annually make the information described in this subsection

 (b) available on its website.

 (a) The commissioner of education shall prepare an annual report on public

 charter schools that includes, at a minimum:

 (1) Public charter school enrollment;

 (2) Geographic distribution of public charter schools; and

 (3) Public charter school performance, as evidenced by the information

 (b) In addition to the annual audit of accounts and records of its approved public

 authorizing report available on its website. The annual authorizing report must include:

 (1) The operating status of the public charter schools approved by the

 authorizer with a designation of:

 (A) Approved, but not yet open;

 (B) Open and operating;

 (C) Revoked, including the reason for revocation;

 (D) Nonrenewed; or

 (E) Closed, including the closing date and reason for closing;

 (2) The oversight and contracted services, if any, provided by the

 authorizer to the public charter schools approved by the authorizer; and

 (3) A performance report for each public charter school it oversees, in

 accordance with the performance framework set forth in the charter agreement.

 SECTION 19. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(a), is amended by

deleting "department of education" and substituting instead "state board of education in

consultation with the commission".

 SECTION 20. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(a), is amended by

adding the following language at the end of the subsection:

 The authorizer shall report each renewal application received by the authorizer to

 the commission no later than ten (10) days from the date on which the authorizer

 received the renewal application.

 SECTION 21. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(d), is amended by

deleting "progress reports" and substituting instead "authorizing report".

 SECTION 22. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(e), is amended by

deleting the subsection.

 SECTION 23. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(f), is amended by

deleting "Beginning immediately upon the repeal of subdivision (e)" and substituting instead

"Beginning on January 1, 2021".

 SECTION 24. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(f)(3), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting instead:

 (3) Notwithstanding subsection (g), the first sentence of § 49-13-110(b), and §

 49-13-110(c), if the commission approves the renewal of a charter agreement on appeal

 from a local board of education, then the public charter school and the commission shall

 enter into a renewed charter agreement in accordance with § 49-13-110(a) for a term of

 no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten (10) academic years, as

 determined by resolution of the commission.

 SECTION 25. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(i), is amended by adding

the language "and commission" after "department of education".

 SECTION 26. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-121(k), is amended by

deleting "department of education" and substituting instead "state board of education".

 ( ) Notwithstanding subsection (g), the first sentence of § 49-13-110(b), and §

 49-13-110(c), if the commission approves the renewal of a charter agreement in

 accordance with § 49-1-614(k)(2)(B) or § 49-1-614(k)(4), then the public charter school

 49-13-110(a) for a term of no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten

 (10) academic years, as determined by resolution of the commission.

adding the language "and commission" after "department of education".

 state board shall create a standard template for purposes of the report and shall post the

 information received from each LEA on its website by December 11 of each year.

 SECTION 30. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-133(b), is amended by

deleting "department" and substituting instead "state board of education".

the section.

deleting "department" wherever it appears and substituting instead "state board".

deleting the second sentence of the subsection and substituting instead:

 If an authorizer has not adopted a performance framework for all of the

 authorizer's schools, then the authorizer must adopt the model performance

 framework developed by the state board pursuant to subsection (a).

 SECTION 34. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 13, is amended by adding

the following new section:

 49-13-137. Replication application.

 (a) A governing body that has at least one (1) public charter school authorized

by a local board of education or by the commission that has been in operation for at

least one (1) full school year at the time the governing body submits its letter of intent

pursuant to § 49-13-107(a) may apply for replication in the LEA in which the governing

body is currently operating to the local board of education or directly to the commission.

The state board of education, in consultation with the commission, shall develop a

replication application form for purposes of this section.

 (b) If the sponsor of the new public charter school by way of replication elects to

apply directly to the commission, then the application process must be conducted in

accordance with § 49-13-107 and with the following:

 (1) The commission shall rule by resolution, at a regularly or specially

 called meeting, to approve or deny a replication application no later than ninety

 (90) days from the date on which the commission received the completed

 application. If the commission fails to approve or deny a replication application

 within ninety (90) days, then the application is deemed approved;

 (2) If the commission denies a replication application, then the grounds

 for denial must be stated in writing and must specify objective reasons for the

 denial. Upon receipt of the grounds for denial, the sponsor has thirty (30) days to

 submit an amended replication application to correct any deficiencies. Upon

 receipt of the amended application, the commission has sixty (60) days to deny

 or approve the amended application. If the commission fails to approve or deny

 the amended application within sixty (60) days, then the amended application is

 deemed approved;

 (3) If the commission approves a replication application, then the

 commission is the authorizer and LEA for that public charter school; and

 (4) The commission's decision is final and not subject to appeal.

 (c) This section does not prohibit a governing body from applying for replication

 to the local board of education through the application process in § 49-13-108(b).

 SECTION 35. The headings in this act are for reference purposes only and do not

constitute a part of the law enacted by this act. However, the Tennessee Code Commission is

requested to include the headings in any compilation or publication containing this act.

 SECTION 36. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.

<summary>
This proposal would change Tennessee's charter school law. It would shift several duties from the department of education to the state board of education and the Tennessee public charter school commission, and it would give the commission more power to approve charter schools directly.

Definitions and applications: The definition of "authorizer" would name local boards of education, the commission, and the achievement school district. A new definition of "replication" would mean opening one or more charter schools with the same academic focus as an existing charter school run by a sponsor or governing body. Sponsors would apply to the local board, or to the commission where the chapter allows direct application. Letters of intent would go to the commission, which must post them on its website within 10 days. Applications would be due February 1 of the year before opening, on a template from the state board in coordination with the commission. Authorizers must report each application to the commission within 10 days.

Direct applications to the commission: Starting July 1, 2025, if the commission overturns a local board's denial three times within three consecutive years, then for the next five years any sponsor in that school district may apply directly to the commission. The commission must rule within 90 days, or the application is deemed approved. If it denies an application, it must give written, objective reasons. The sponsor then has 30 days to amend, and the commission has 60 days to decide, or the amended application is deemed approved. If it approves, the commission becomes both authorizer and local education agency for that school. Its decision is final and cannot be appealed. After the five years, sponsors must apply to the local board again unless the conditions are met again.

Higher education: Public colleges and universities in Tennessee could apply to the local board or directly to the commission. A charter school they sponsor could give enrollment preference to children of their employees or governing board members, up to 25% of total enrollment.

Replication: A governing body with at least one charter school that has operated a full school year could apply to replicate in its current district, either to the local board or directly to the commission. The state board, in consultation with the commission, would create the application form. The direct-to-commission process uses the same 90-day, 30-day, and 60-day deadlines, deemed-approval rules, written-denial rules, commission-as-authorizer rule, and no-appeal rule. Applying to the local board through the existing process would remain allowed.

Amendments, renewals, and reports: The commission would set timelines and the appeal process for charter amendment petitions, and its denials of amendments could not be appealed. Governing bodies could petition for voluntary early termination. Authorizers must report renewal applications to the commission within 10 days. If the commission approves a renewal on appeal, or in certain achievement school district situations, the renewed charter would last at least five and no more than ten academic years, set by commission resolution. The commissioner of education would produce an annual charter school report. Each authorizer would send an annual report by January 1 to the state board and post it online. It would cover each school's status, services the authorizer provided, and a performance report. The commission would post certain annual information online. Local districts that collect authorizer fees must report amounts and uses to the state board by December 1, and the state board would post them by December 11. The state board would also provide the model performance framework, which authorizers without their own must adopt.

Other changes: Several references would change from the department to the state board or commission, a provision on charter school requirements would be deleted, and section 49-13-142 would be repealed. Some provisions would start January 1, 2021. The act takes effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

claims.claim: Tennessee public colleges and universities may apply to the local board or directly to the commission.
claims.summary_quote: Public colleges and universities in Tennessee could apply to the local board or directly to the commission.
claims.source_quote:
A public institution of higher education in this state that seeks to open

a public charter school may apply to the local board of education or directly to the

commission.
claims.rationale: This is a plain-language description of the eligible public institutions.

claims.claim: Schools sponsored by those institutions may prefer children of their employees or governing-body members in enrollment.
claims.summary_quote: A charter school they sponsor could give enrollment preference to children of their employees or governing board members
claims.source_quote:
a public charter school sponsored

by a public institution of higher education in this state may give an enrollment

preference to children of the public institution of higher education's employees or

members of the institution's governing body
claims.rationale: The permission and beneficiary groups match.

claims.claim: The higher-education enrollment preference is capped at twenty-five percent of total enrollment.
claims.summary_quote: up to 25% of total enrollment
claims.source_quote:
not to exceed twenty-five percent

(25%) of the public charter school's total enrollment.
claims.rationale: The numerical cap matches.

claims.claim: Having a charter school that has operated for one full school year is sufficient to qualify a governing body for replication.
claims.summary_quote: A governing body with at least one charter school that has operated a full school year could apply to replicate
claims.source_quote:
A governing body that has at least one (1) public charter school authorized

by a local board of education or by the commission that has been in operation for at

least one (1) full school year at the time the governing body submits its letter of intent
claims.rationale: The stated eligibility rule drops both the qualifying authorizer requirement and the requirement to complete that year before submitting the letter of intent.

claims.claim: Replication applications may be made in the governing body's current district to either the local board or the commission.
claims.summary_quote: in its current district, either to the local board or directly to the commission
claims.source_quote:
may apply for replication in the LEA in which the governing

body is currently operating to the local board of education or directly to the commission.
claims.rationale: The location and alternative recipients match.

claims.claim: The state board must develop the replication application form in consultation with the commission.
claims.summary_quote: The state board, in consultation with the commission, would create the application form.
claims.source_quote:
The state board of education, in consultation with the commission, shall develop a

replication application form for purposes of this section.
claims.rationale: The responsible actor and consultation requirement are explicit.

claims.claim: Direct replication applications have a ninety-day initial decision deadline.
claims.summary_quote: The direct-to-commission process uses the same 90-day, 30-day, and 60-day deadlines
claims.source_quote:
approve or deny a replication application no later than ninety

 (90) days from the date on which the commission received the completed

 application.
claims.rationale: The replication process uses the stated initial deadline.

claims.claim: Replication applicants have thirty days after receiving denial grounds to amend.
claims.summary_quote: The direct-to-commission process uses the same 90-day, 30-day, and 60-day deadlines
claims.source_quote:
Upon receipt of the grounds for denial, the sponsor has thirty (30) days to

 submit an amended replication application to correct any deficiencies.
claims.rationale: The replication amendment deadline matches.

claims.claim: The commission has sixty days to decide amended replication applications.
claims.summary_quote: The direct-to-commission process uses the same 90-day, 30-day, and 60-day deadlines
claims.source_quote:
Upon

 receipt of the amended application, the commission has sixty (60) days to deny

 or approve the amended application.
claims.rationale: The amended-application decision deadline matches.

claims.claim: Missing the initial replication deadline produces deemed approval.
claims.summary_quote: deemed-approval rules
claims.source_quote:
If the commission fails to approve or deny a replication application

 within ninety (90) days, then the application is deemed approved;
claims.rationale: The initial deemed-approval rule is explicit.

claims.claim: Missing the amended replication deadline produces deemed approval.
claims.summary_quote: deemed-approval rules
claims.rationale: The amended-application deemed-approval rule is explicit.

claims.claim: Replication denials must state objective reasons in writing.
claims.summary_quote: written-denial rules
claims.source_quote:
If the commission denies a replication application, then the grounds

 for denial must be stated in writing and must specify objective reasons for the

 denial.
claims.rationale: The referenced denial requirements match those previously summarized.

claims.claim: Approval of replication makes the commission the school's authorizer.
claims.summary_quote: commission-as-authorizer rule
claims.source_quote:
If the commission approves a replication application, then the

 commission is the authorizer and LEA for that public charter school;
claims.rationale: The commission becomes the authorizer upon approval.

claims.claim: The commission's replication decision cannot be appealed.
claims.summary_quote: no-appeal rule
claims.source_quote: The commission's decision is final and not subject to appeal.
claims.rationale: Section 34 expressly bars appeals.

claims.claim: Replication through the local-board application process remains allowed.
claims.summary_quote: Applying to the local board through the existing process would remain allowed.
claims.source_quote:
This section does not prohibit a governing body from applying for replication

to the local board of education through the application process in § 49-13-108(b).
claims.rationale: The bill expressly preserves this route.

claims.claim: The commission would establish charter-amendment approval timelines and the appeal process.
claims.summary_quote: The commission would set timelines and the appeal process for charter amendment petitions
claims.source_quote:
The commission shall determine the timelines for

 approval and the appeal process.
claims.rationale: The duty is expressly assigned to the commission.

claims.claim: The commission's denials of amendment petitions cannot be appealed.
claims.summary_quote: its denials of amendments could not be appealed
claims.source_quote:
If the authorizer is the commission, then an appeal

 shall not be made of the commission's decision to deny a petition to amend the charter

 agreement.
claims.rationale: In this petition-to-authorizer context, the summary accurately describes commission denials.

claims.claim: Governing bodies may petition for voluntary termination before a charter agreement expires.
claims.summary_quote: Governing bodies could petition for voluntary early termination.
claims.source_quote:
The governing body of a public charter school may petition the authorizer

 for voluntary termination of the charter agreement before the charter agreement expires.
claims.rationale: The permission and early-termination scope match.

claims.claim: Authorizers must report renewal applications to the commission within ten days.
claims.summary_quote: Authorizers must report renewal applications to the commission within 10 days.
claims.source_quote:
The authorizer shall report each renewal application received by the authorizer to

 the commission no later than ten (10) days from the date on which the authorizer

 received the renewal application.
claims.rationale: The actor, recipient, and deadline match.

claims.claim: Commission approval of a renewal on appeal from a local board requires a renewed charter of five to ten academic years.
claims.summary_quote: If the commission approves a renewal on appeal, or in certain achievement school district situations, the renewed charter would last at least five and no more than ten academic years
claims.source_quote:
if the commission approves the renewal of a charter agreement on appeal

 from a local board of education, then the public charter school and the commission shall

 enter into a renewed charter agreement in accordance with § 49-13-110(a) for a term of

 no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten (10) academic years
claims.rationale: The appeal-renewal term range is explicit.

claims.claim: The additional renewal circumstances concern achievement school district situations.
claims.summary_quote: or in certain achievement school district situations
claims.source_quote:
if the commission approves the renewal of a charter agreement in

 accordance with § 49-1-614(k)(2)(B) or § 49-1-614(k)(4)
claims.rationale: The bill gives statutory cross-references but does not reproduce the circumstances they govern.

claims.claim: Renewals under the additional cited provisions also require terms of five to ten academic years.
claims.summary_quote: the renewed charter would last at least five and no more than ten academic years
claims.source_quote:
then the public charter school

 and the commission shall enter into a renewed charter agreement in accordance with §

 49-13-110(a) for a term of no less than five (5) academic years, but no more than ten

 (10) academic years
claims.rationale: Section 27 expressly sets this range for the additional cross-referenced renewals.

claims.claim: The commission sets these renewal terms by resolution.
claims.summary_quote: set by commission resolution
claims.source_quote: as determined by resolution of the commission.
claims.rationale: Both renewal provisions contain this requirement.

claims.claim: The commissioner of education must prepare an annual charter-school report.
claims.summary_quote: The commissioner of education would produce an annual charter school report.
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner of education shall prepare an annual report on public

 charter schools
claims.rationale: The reporting actor and frequency match.

claims.claim: Each authorizer must submit an annual report to the state board by January 1.
claims.summary_quote: Each authorizer would send an annual report by January 1 to the state board
claims.source_quote:
each authorizer shall, by January 1 each year,

 submit an annual authorizing report to the state board of education
claims.rationale: The recipient and deadline match.

claims.claim: Each authorizer must post its annual authorizing report online.
claims.summary_quote: and post it online
claims.source_quote:
make the annual

 authorizing report available on its website.
claims.rationale: Website publication is required.

claims.claim: The authorizing report must include school operating statuses.
claims.summary_quote: It would cover each school's status
claims.source_quote:
The operating status of the public charter schools approved by the

 authorizer
claims.rationale: Operating status is a required report element.

claims.claim: The authorizing report must include services supplied by the authorizer.
claims.summary_quote: services the authorizer provided
claims.source_quote:
The oversight and contracted services, if any, provided by the

 authorizer to the public charter schools approved by the authorizer
claims.rationale: The summary accurately condenses the services reporting requirement.

claims.claim: The authorizing report must include a performance report.
claims.summary_quote: and a performance report
claims.source_quote:
A performance report for each public charter school it oversees, in

 accordance with the performance framework set forth in the charter agreement.
claims.rationale: Performance reporting is expressly required.

claims.claim: The commission must annually publish certain information online.
claims.summary_quote: The commission would post certain annual information online.
claims.source_quote:
The commission shall annually make the information described in this subsection

 (b) available on its website.
claims.rationale: The summary does not assert unreproduced details about that information.

claims.claim: Districts collecting annual authorizer fees must report the amounts collected and authorizing obligations funded to the state board by December 1.
claims.summary_quote: Local districts that collect authorizer fees must report amounts and uses to the state board by December 1
claims.source_quote:
By December 1 of each year, each LEA that collects an annual authorizer fee

 shall report the total amount of authorizer fees collected in the previous school year and

 the authorizing obligations fulfilled using the fee to the state board of education.
claims.rationale: The collection condition, reporting content, recipient, and deadline match.

claims.claim: The state board must publish the fee information by December 11.
claims.summary_quote: the state board would post them by December 11
claims.source_quote:
shall post the

 information received from each LEA on its website by December 11 of each year.
claims.rationale: The posting deadline is explicit.

claims.claim: The state board would develop the model performance framework.
claims.summary_quote: The state board would also provide the model performance framework
claims.source_quote:
the model performance

 framework developed by the state board pursuant to subsection (a).
claims.rationale: The replacement text identifies the state board as the framework's developer.

claims.claim: Authorizers without their own performance framework must adopt the state-board model.
claims.summary_quote: which authorizers without their own must adopt
claims.source_quote:
If an authorizer has not adopted a performance framework for all of the

 authorizer's schools, then the authorizer must adopt the model performance

 framework
claims.rationale: Authorizers without a framework fall within the express adoption requirement.

claims.source_quote:
SECTION 15. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-116(a), is amended by

deleting "department" and substituting instead "state board".

 SECTION 16. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-116(b), is amended by

claims.rationale: Sections 8 and 23 insert that beginning date; the summary separately states the act's effective date.
